abstract: Extended reality (XR) enables controlled yet naturalistic multisensory experiments, but its validity depends on whether virtualized cues are perceptually plausible and lead to behavior comparable to the real world. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to perceptually evaluate a six-degree-of-freedom (6DoF) XR system that combines real-time room acoustic simulation, binaural rendering, and an audio-visually matched virtual replica of a large laboratory room in terms of both plausibility and behavior. In two experiments with 45 participants, we investigated how auditory and visual virtualization affect plausibility and dynamic auditory distance perception (ADP). A plausibility experiment compared real and virtual sound sources in audio-augmented reality (AAR) and virtual reality (VR), while a locomotion-based ADP experiment assessed distance-judgment accuracy, signed error, and task effort across four virtualization conditions. The system produced plausible binaural rendering in both AAR and VR, with higher plausibility in VR, indicating that perceptual requirements for XR audio depend on the visual reference frame. In the ADP task, any form of virtualization reduced accuracy and increased effort, although performance remained high overall. Virtual audio produced a bias toward nearer perceived source distances, whereas visual-only virtualization reduced accuracy without a significant directional bias. These effects did not add up in full VR. Overall, the findings demonstrate the strong potential of current 6DoF XR systems for interactive perceptual research, while revealing that task-specific behavioral validation may be necessary.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文用同一套 6 自由度视听系统比较真实与虚拟条件，说明实时房间声学仿真加双耳渲染在听觉增强现实与虚拟现实中都能让人难辨真假、且虚拟现实更难辨，但任何一种虚拟化都会让走动中的距离辨认准确率下降约 5 个百分点并增加努力感，其中只有虚拟听觉带来系统性的偏近偏差。
originalTitle: Auditory and Visual Virtualization in 6DoF XR: Effects on Plausibility and Dynamic Auditory Distance Perception
readerTitle: 在能走动的 XR 里听距离：逼真感与动态听觉距离判断如何被虚拟化改变
